=== FINDINGS FROM mistralai_mistral-small-2603 ===
- File: scripts/write_guard.sh
  Line or code reference: write_guard_check function, lines 79-82 (bypass audit), 206-212 (block logs), ~117 (Python inline block)
  Problem: WRITE_GUARD_BYPASS_ENV and WRITE_GUARD_BLOCK log lines emit raw, unsanitized values for environment variables and file paths, which can contain newlines, tabs, or whitespace that corrupt the single-line stable log prefix format defined in agents.md.
  Why it fails at runtime: GitHub Actions workflow logs and downstream parsing tools rely on the stable single-line prefix format for log markers like `WRITE_GUARD_BLOCK: phase=review_editor path=.github/workflows/test.yml...`. When variables contain control characters, the log entry can span multiple lines, breaking parsers and losing audit visibility.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: scripts/write_guard.sh
  Line or code reference: write_guard_check, lines 193-199 (JSON parse errors)
  Problem: When JSON parse or schema validation fails (rc=2), the handler uses a generic CONFIG_ERROR message without distinguishing the specific failure mode (missing file vs malformed JSON vs unsupported schema).
  Why it fails at runtime: Operators lose diagnostic detail needed to debug configuration issues in `.github/ai/write_guards.v1.json`, potentially causing repeated failures during deployment.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===
- File: scripts/write_guard.sh
  Line or code reference: lines ~206-212 (WRITE_GUARD_BLOCK echo inside the violations while-read loop)
  Problem: path, pattern, env_var, and env_value are echoed directly into WRITE_GUARD_BLOCK log lines without any sanitization. While write_guard_sanitize_log_value() exists (line ~25) and is used for write_guard_detail in the CONFIG_ERROR path, it is not applied to the block-audit fields.
  Why it fails at runtime: If any of these values contain tabs or newlines (e.g. a malicious env value or an edge-case path), the tab-delimited while-read split in the bash wrapper would produce misaligned fields, and downstream stable-prefix log parsers expecting single-line WRITE_GUARD_BLOCK entries would break.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/write_guard.sh
  Line or code reference: line ~81 (WRITE_GUARD_BYPASS_ENV echo in the bypass path)
  Problem: write_guard_enabled_value is echoed directly without sanitization via write_guard_sanitize_log_value().
  Why it fails at runtime: WRITE_GUARDS_ENABLED could contain whitespace or control characters if set through unusual means; the embedded control chars would break the single-line WRITE_GUARD_BYPASS_ENV log prefix contract.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===
